alerts.title: Overdue creatinine monitoring on TDF
alerts.message: Guidelines require serum creatinine and eGFR every 12 months for patients on TDF. The patient's last creatinine was 478 days ago, exceeding the 12-month interval. No creatinine was ordered at today's visit. TDF can cause renal toxicity including chronic kidney disease and Fanconi syndrome. No symptoms or examination findings suggest renal dysfunction, but early TDF nephrotoxicity may be asymptomatic. A current creatinine and eGFR are needed to assess ongoing renal safety.

evidence.recommended_action: Order serum creatinine and eGFR now; the last result is over 12 months old. Continue annual renal monitoring while on TDF.

alerts.title: Viral load near detection threshold
alerts.message: Guidelines state viral load should be measured 6 months after ART initiation and every 6–12 months. The latest viral load is 40 copies/mL, which is detectable but below the 1000 copies/mL treatment-failure threshold. This low-level viremia may represent a blip or early adherence issues. The clinician's plan does not address the detectable result. Repeat viral load testing should be considered to confirm whether this is transient or a rising trend.

evidence.recommended_action: Repeat viral load within 3–6 months to confirm suppression, and reinforce adherence counseling given the detectable result.
